conventional_description: In Western medicine, the inability to ejaculate despite adequate stimulation is classified as anejaculation. It is often distinguished from retrograde ejaculation, where semen travels backward into the bladder. The cause may be psychological, such as performance anxiety or relationship issues, or physical, such as nerve damage from surgery, spinal cord injury, diabetes, or certain medications. Diagnosis typically involves a detailed sexual history, physical examination, and sometimes post-ejaculatory urinalysis to rule out retrograde ejaculation.
conventional_treatments: Conventional treatment depends on the underlying cause. If a medication is responsible, a doctor may adjust the dose or switch to an alternative. Psychological factors are addressed with sex therapy, counseling, or cognitive behavioral approaches. For nerve-related causes, vibratory stimulation or electrical stimulation may be used to trigger the ejaculatory reflex. In some cases, medications that affect the nervous system may be prescribed to facilitate ejaculation.
tcm_understanding: TCM understands the ejaculatory process as a coordinated event that requires two main forces to work in harmony. The Kidney system provides the foundational power: Kidney Yang supplies the warmth and drive to open the seminal gate, while Kidney Yin supplies the nourishing essence and lubrication. When this system is depleted, ejaculation becomes impossible despite normal desire and erection. This is why overwork, excessive sexual activity, or chronic illness can gradually drain the reserves needed for this final release.
classical_quote: 「肾主骨髓，而藏于精。虚劳肾气虚弱，故精液泄而不能射。」
classical_translation: "The Kidney governs the bones and marrow and stores the essence. In consumptive fatigue, the Kidney Qi becomes weak and vacuous, therefore the essence fluid leaks [in dreams] but cannot be shot out [during intercourse]."
classical_source:
诸病源候论 (Zhu Bing Yuan Hou Lun)  ,  Volume 4, Treatise on Empty-Taxation Seminal Emission 									·
More references
tcm_diagnosis:
A practitioner usually begins by asking what the experience actually feels like and what other signs accompany it. The presence of strong desire and an erection that stays firm points away from Kidney Yang deficiency and more toward either Yin deficiency with heat or a blockage pattern. The tongue and pulse are the next essential clues.
If the person feels restless, has a dry mouth, and the tongue appears red with little or no coating, that suggests Kidney Yin Deficiency with Empty-Heat Blazing. The pulse will feel thin and rapid. This pattern often arises from overwork or excessive sexual activity that has drained the body's cooling, nourishing resources.
When emotional frustration and stress are the backdrop, with a sensation of chest or rib-side tightness, the pattern is more likely Liver Qi Stagnation transforming into Heat. The tongue tip may look redder than the rest, and the pulse feels wiry. This heat disturbs the Heart and Liver connection that governs release.
If the person has a heavy sensation in the body, a bitter taste in the mouth, and urine that looks dark or turbid, Damp-Heat in the Lower Burner is the key suspect. The tongue coating will be yellow and greasy, and the pulse will feel slippery and rapid. This pattern is common with a rich diet or alcohol use.
In cases with a clear history of physical trauma, surgery, or a very chronic timeline, Blood Stagnation may be the root. The tongue may show dark spots or a purplish hue, and the pulse will feel choppy or wiry. The local sensation is often one of distension or pain in the pelvic area.
For a person who feels generally depleted, with pale complexion, low back weakness, and a mix of dry and cold signs, a Deficiency of both Kidney Yin and Yang is the more complex picture. The tongue may be pale with a thin coating, and the pulse is often fine and weak. This pattern reflects a long-standing, deep exhaustion of the body's reserves.

patterns.pattern_name: Kidney Yin Deficiency With Empty-Heat Blazing
patterns.symptoms: ["Strong sexual desire with inability to ejaculate", "Night sweats", "Five-palm heat (heat in palms, soles, and chest)", "Dry mouth and throat, especially at night", "Irritability and mental restlessness", "Lower back soreness"]
patterns.worse_with: Stress and frustration, Spicy, greasy, or fried foods, Alcohol, Overwork and late nights, Hot weather or sauna, Excessive sexual activity
patterns.better_with: Cooling foods like pear, cucumber, and tofu, Adequate rest and sleep, Cool environment, Relaxation practices, Moderate, gentle exercise
patterns.why_this_happens: Excessive sexual activity or masturbation gradually burns through the Kidney's cooling Yin reserves, leaving behind a relative excess of heat. This empty-heat agitates the body, keeping the penis engorged and desire strong, but the depleted Yin fails to anchor the essence and open the seminal gate. The result is a frustrating inability to ejaculate despite normal or even heightened arousal.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red, thin, and dry with little or no coating, possibly cracked. Pulse: fine (细 xì) and rapid (数 shuò), weak at the rear (Kidney) position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Empty-heat flares up when Yin is thin, so anything that adds heat-spicy food, alcohol, emotional stress, or a hot environment-makes the agitation worse. Overwork and late nights further drain Yin, leaving even less substance to anchor the heat. Cooling foods, rest, and a calm environment help replenish Yin and settle the fire, allowing the essence gate to function normally again.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Prioritize cooling, Yin-nourishing foods like pear, cucumber, black sesame, and tofu. Avoid spicy, greasy, or fried foods, and cut back on alcohol and coffee. Go to bed before 11 p.m. and protect sleep quality; moderate, gentle exercise like walking or tai chi supports Yin without overheating the body.

patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Kidney Yang is like the body's pilot light. Cold extinguishes it, whether it comes from the weather, raw foods, or iced drinks. Exhaustion and overwork deplete the Kidneys further, while rest and warmth gently feed the fire. Warmth on the lower back, where the Kidneys reside, and warm, cooked foods directly support the Yang needed to power the ejaculatory mechanism.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Eat warming, cooked foods like soups and stews. Add a little ginger or cinnamon to meals. Avoid raw, cold foods and iced drinks, which further dampen the digestive fire. Gentle daily movement, like a walk, helps warm the body without exhausting it. Keep the lower back warm with a hot water bottle or a belly band.

patterns.pattern_name: Liver Qi Stagnation that transforms into Heat
patterns.symptoms: ["Strong sexual desire with inability to ejaculate", "Irritability and mental restlessness", "Distending pain in the ribcage", "Bitter taste in the mouth"]
patterns.worse_with: Stress and frustration, Anger or resentment, Spicy, greasy, or fried foods, Alcohol, Emotional suppression
patterns.better_with: Moderate, gentle exercise, Expressing emotions openly, Cooling foods like pear, cucumber, and tofu, Calm, pressure-free environment
patterns.why_this_happens: When frustration, resentment, or unexpressed anger build up, the Liver's ability to keep Qi flowing smoothly breaks down. That stagnant Qi smolders and generates Heat, which travels upward to disturb the Heart and agitate the mind. In this pattern, the normal ejaculatory reflex is blocked not by weakness, but by a tense, overheated state where the release mechanism becomes locked shut. Sexual desire may be normal or even heightened, but the explosive, frustrated tension prevents completion.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body with redder sides and a yellow coating. Pulse: wiry and rapid (弦数, xián shuò), most pronounced at the left middle position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: The core of this pattern is Qi that is stuck and has overheated. Stress, anger, and emotional suppression directly worsen the stagnation, which is the physical root of the blocked ejaculation. Spicy foods and alcohol add more heat to an already overheated system. Gentle exercise and emotional expression physically move Liver Qi, while cooling foods and a calm environment help clear the pathological heat, allowing the release mechanism to relax and function.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid spicy, fried, and greasy foods that add heat to the body. Gentle daily exercise like walking or yoga helps move stagnant Liver Qi. Crucially, find a healthy outlet for frustration and communicate openly with your partner to release emotional tension.

patterns.why_this_happens: Dampness and Heat are heavy, sticky pathogens that naturally sink downward. A diet rich in greasy or spicy foods and alcohol brews this turbid mix internally, which then pours into the lower body. This inflammatory sludge congests the seminal tract, physically gumming up the passageway and preventing ejaculation even when sexual desire stays strong. The normal urge is there, but the plumbing is blocked by the hot, sticky obstruction.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body with a thick, yellow, greasy coating that is most prominent at the back. Pulse: slippery (滑 huá) and rapid (数 shuò), especially noticeable at the rear (Chi) position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Alcohol and greasy, spicy foods are the very substances that create Dampness and Heat in the body, directly feeding this pattern. A hot, humid climate adds external dampness to internal dampness, worsening the blockage. Sitting for long hours compresses the lower body and stagnates Qi, which allows the heavy, sticky Dampness to settle. Bitter, cooling foods and a clean diet work because they literally drain the pathological Damp-Heat from the Lower Burner, removing the sludge that is obstructing the seminal tract.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Adopt a clean, cooling diet centered on lightly cooked vegetables and grains. Strictly avoid alcohol, deep-fried foods, and sugary drinks which create more internal Dampness. Bitter greens like dandelion and celery help drain Damp-Heat naturally. Gentle, regular exercise helps move stagnant Qi and dry out excess moisture, but avoid overexertion in humid environments.

When Qi flow becomes stuck over a long period, or after a physical injury or surgery in the pelvic area, the blood stops moving freely and forms a kind of internal obstruction. This is like a traffic jam in the channels that carry semen outward, so even with normal desire and arousal, the release simply cannot get through.

Emotional frustration, especially suppressed anger, tightens the Liver Qi and worsens the stagnation. Gentle movement and warmth help soften and open the blocked channels, allowing the physical obstruction to gradually dissolve.

Include small amounts of blood-moving spices like turmeric and saffron in your cooking, and stay away from very cold or raw foods that can congeal the blood.

faqs.question: Is this the same as retrograde ejaculation?
faqs.answer: No, they are different. In retrograde ejaculation, the semen is produced but travels backward into the bladder instead of out through the urethra. In anejaculation (the focus here), the ejaculatory reflex itself is not triggered. TCM can sometimes help with retrograde ejaculation, but it requires a different diagnostic approach focused on the strength of the Kidney's grasping function.

faqs.question: Can acupuncture and herbs really help with anejaculation?
faqs.answer: Yes, many men find significant help from TCM, especially when the cause is functional rather than a complete nerve severance. The key is a correct pattern diagnosis. For example, a man with Kidney Yin deficiency and heat would receive a very different treatment from a man with Kidney Yang deficiency, even though both cannot ejaculate. When the right pattern is treated, the ejaculatory reflex can be restored.

faqs.question: I have strong erections but cannot ejaculate. My partner feels frustrated. Can TCM help?
faqs.answer: This is a classic presentation of Yin deficiency with empty heat - the heat keeps you aroused and erect, but the Yin substance needed to anchor the release is depleted. TCM has specific formulas like Zhi Bo Di Huang Wan to nourish the Yin and cool the heat. With consistent treatment, the body can regain its ability to complete the sexual response cycle.

faqs.question: I have normal desire but feel too exhausted to reach ejaculation. What does TCM say?
faqs.answer: This often points to Kidney Yang deficiency, where the body's warming and propulsive power is too weak to push the semen out. You might also notice a cold, aching lower back and a general feeling of being chilled. Treatment focuses on warming and strengthening the Kidney Yang with formulas like You Gui Wan and moxibustion on specific acupuncture points.

faqs.question: Can stress and anger really block ejaculation?
faqs.answer: Yes. In TCM, the Liver is responsible for the smooth flow of Qi and blood throughout the body, including the reproductive organs. When stress, frustration, or resentment cause Liver Qi to stagnate, it can create a kind of internal traffic jam that blocks the ejaculatory reflex. This is why some men cannot ejaculate specifically when feeling pressured or angry.

faqs.question: Will I need to make big changes to my diet?
faqs.answer: Basic dietary adjustments can be very supportive. If your pattern is one of heat or damp-heat, avoiding spicy, greasy foods and alcohol is crucial. For deficiency patterns, eating warm, nourishing cooked foods is helpful. Your practitioner will guide you on the specifics, but the changes are usually manageable and part of the holistic treatment.

faqs.question: How long until I see results with TCM?
faqs.answer: Many men begin to notice changes in their overall energy, mood, and comfort within the first few weeks. For the ejaculatory function itself, patterns of stagnation or heat often respond within a month or two. If the pattern is one of deep deficiency, rebuilding the body's reserves to the point of consistent ejaculation can take three to six months of steady treatment.

research.title: Clinical observation on acupuncture treatment of functional anejaculation
research.description: This study observed the effects of acupuncture on men with functional anejaculation. After a course of treatment with points including Zhongji REN-3 and Sanyinjiao SP-6, a significant number of patients were able to achieve ejaculation during intercourse. The study concluded that acupuncture is an effective and safe treatment for this condition.

research.description: A clinical report on 30 men with anejaculation treated with a modified Long Dan Xie Gan Tang formula. The treatment targeted Liver Qi stagnation transforming into heat. The report found a high overall effectiveness rate, with most patients achieving normal ejaculation after a course of herbal therapy, highlighting the efficacy of this classic formula for this specific pattern.
